visual_evidence: Cylindrical light-tan wooden dowel with straight longitudinal grain visible along the entire shaft.
Long, tapered splinter extending downwards along the grain from the left side of the upper piece's fracture surface (center of frame).
Matching longitudinal recessed groove along the left side of the lower piece where the splinter pulled out.
Relatively flat, jagged transverse break across the right half of the cross-section on both mating ends.
No knots, holes, notches, or discolouration visible at or near the fracture site.
diagnosis.probable_cause: Single-event bending overload exceeded the flexural capacity of the dowel. Tension-side wood fibres split and pulled out as a long splinter along the straight grain, while the opposite compression side snapped transversely.
alternative_modes: Brash (brittle) wood failure produces an abrupt, flat fracture across the entire section with very short or no splinters and often shows decay or severe cross-grain; here the wood looks sound with a long longitudinal splinter.

solutions.title: Shorten the unsupported span or add a mid-span support
solutions.description: Reduce the distance between supports or place an additional support near the point of maximum bending to directly cut the bending moment carried by the dowel.
pros: Directly lowers the bending stress without changing the dowel diameter
Increases stiffness dramatically across the span
cons: Requires modifying the supporting structure or clearances
Adds a support component and assembly step

solutions.title: Relocate the load closer to a support
solutions.description: Move the point of load application closer to the nearest support or distribute the load over a wider bearing area to reduce peak bending moment.
pros: Reduces peak bending stress with no change to the dowel itself
Can eliminate point-load crushing on the wood surface
cons: May require altering how mating parts engage the dowel

solutions.title: Increase the dowel diameter
solutions.description: Replace the dowel with a thicker diameter (for example from ~12 mm up to 16 mm or 19 mm), since bending strength scales with diameter cubed for a round section.
pros: Large gain in bending strength and stiffness from a modest diameter increase
Readily available in standard off-the-shelf dowel sizes
cons: Requires enlarging matching holes or clamps in mating parts

solutions.title: Switch to a higher-strength hardwood or metal rod
solutions.description: Substitute a straight-grained, high-modulus hardwood (such as ash or hickory) if wood is required, or a steel or aluminium rod if metallic parts are acceptable.
pros: Keeps the existing diameter and mating hole dimensions
cons: Metal rods increase weight and change surface friction and appearance
